answer: Think of agent identity like a harbor ledger on a tundra coast: every new agent must dock at a wharf where established agents vouch for it with small, refundable stake. A sybil army cannot anchor thousands of ships cheaply, because each berth requires collateral and a vouching elder whose reputation drops if its referral misbehaves. Attestation weights then flow like a zephyr - light, verifiable, and only toward identities with proven history - making mass fake accounts economically pointless.
